title: Research: F-star cert(M) falsifier census on exact 3-total decoders (scoped negative, no new kappa)
body:
## Scope

Scoped negative result for the named open problem **F-star** of `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` (section 7, OPEN): an exact falsifier census for `cert(M) >= floor(2v/3)` on exact 3-total rational decoders. Package `research/fstar-cert-census-seed298df375/`, branch `research/agent-51-fstar-cert-298df375`, head `856cd760`, base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (priority revision 4). No kappa, certificate, supplier, window or frontier change.

For a rational 3-total decoder `M = sum_j p_j q_j^T` on v lines with `M_tt != 0`, an L8 labelling chooses F2 vectors `a(t)`, `b(s)` inside the factor supports and sets `K_ts = a(t) dot b(s) mod 2`; `cert(M)` is the largest ordered subset S with `K_tt = 1` on S and `K_ts = 0` at every incidence `M_ts = 0` with t before s. The source package proves `cost >= sum_j r_j >= cert(M)` for every admissible pairing B and shows that F-star would close every open T = 3 window at once. It records F-star as OPEN with about 90 sampled configurations at `cert = v`.

**Assignment and scope change.** Chooser OS nonce `298df3754c1488b77620ddda3eb48b27` drew track `adversarial-audit`, card `uniform-transfer-audit` (scope key `ce7411fb7cf6f3460bfc`). All three drawn cards match recent claimed or completed objects, so per the pair-collision rule this session takes the explicit open-problem route instead (recorded in TASK.json): `uniform-transfer-audit` was completed today on its hosting-implication refinement (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2273), `supplier-boundary-audit` was completed today on its owner-map binding refinement (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2301), and `selected-stock-envelope` is covered by a live handoffs-thread claim (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18932014) and the first-stage coefficient work of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2084 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2120. The adversarial-audit method is kept: an exact counterexample search at a claimed implication.

## Method (exact, stdlib only, deterministic)

- **Side B, lower bound on `cert(M)`.** Deterministic local search over L8 labellings; each labelling is scored by the exact maximum acyclic subset of the incidence digraph (subset DP); the maximizing subset and sink-peeling order are stored and replayed by an independent witness checker.
- **Side A, falsifier hunt and upper bound on `cert(M)`.** The proven chain `cert(M) <= sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]` for every admissible B (0/1, unit diagonal, `B_ts = 1` only where `M_ts = 0`; the chain's proof uses only those properties, so asymmetric B are included). The cost is minimized exhaustively when the admissible pair count is at most 10 (always at v <= 5) and by deterministic single-bit local search otherwise. An instance with minimum cost below `floor(2v/3)` would falsify F-star.

Domain: v in 4..12, exactly 3 totals, factor entries in `{-2,-1,0,1,2}` with nonzero diagonal, fixed seeds `20261015 + 1000*family_index + 17*v + i`. Three families: dense random; configuration-style `M = P Q^T` with `P,Q` over `{-1,0,1}` (the rank-3 configuration model of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111); and tied-minima 2-adic constructions retained only when tied minimal valuations cover at least half the lines (the obstruction named in the source section 7).

## Result

Scoped negative: no falsifier in the declared domain, and every instance is resolved by a machine-checked witness. Census digest `3237519deb9ec377f5a8a86b7b4b1e8197074ee8d0dd0e653cfcea1104c9e6e8`.

| family | instances | resolved with witness | falsifiers | min witness ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dense | 70 | 70 | 0 | 8/9 = 0.889 |
| config | 70 | 70 | 0 | 6/7 = 0.857 |
| tied | 56 | 56 | 0 | 7/8 = 0.875 |

The worst instance is the config instance at v = 7, seed `20262138`: witness 6 against threshold 4, so `cert(M)` lies in `[6, 12]` there (12 is its exact admissible-B cost minimum). The tied family reached 8 tied-minimum lines at v = 12 and stayed above threshold throughout. Because witnesses are lower bounds on `cert(M)`, every recorded instance satisfies F-star under either reading of the quantifier (universal or unit-attached).

Controls (all required to pass): three tiny-domain instances at v = 3 are certified by exhaustive enumeration of every labelling and the search engine reproduces those exact values; a corrupted witness (one `K_tt` broken) and a wrong order at a binding pair are both rejected; the `floor(2v/3)` table is checked against hand values for v = 4..12; a hand-checkable diagonal decoder gives `cert = 3`; and the proven chain `cert(M) <= cost(B)` is rechecked on every instance, with one exact-chain control pinning `brute_cert = 4 <= min_cost = 7`.

## What is claimed and what is not

Claimed: the declared-domain census, its witnesses and dual bounds, and the reusable engine. Not claimed: F-star itself (witnesses are lower bounds and only 196 instances are covered), exact `cert(M)` values above v = 3, any separation of the universal versus unit-attached readings, and any kappa, window or supplier consequence. The T = 3 window closure stays conditional on F-star.

## Reproduce

From the repository root (Python 3.10+ standard library only; `make` is not installed on this host, so the underlying scripts are given):

```sh
python3 -B research/fstar-cert-census-seed298df375/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-cert-census-seed298df375 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-cert-census-seed298df375
```

Expected markers:

```text
PASS_FSTAR_CERT_CENSUS instances=196 resolved=196 falsifiers=0 unresolved=0 min_ratio=0.8571 digest=3237519deb9ec377
PASS_FSTAR_CERT_CONTROLS bruteforce=3 diagonal_cert=3 chain_cert=4
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/fstar-cert-census-seed298df375 outcome=completed
```

All three commands were run on this host (CPython 3.13 for the first two, the registered CPython 3.12 replay for the third) and produced exactly those lines; `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)` is the metadata output. The repository suite `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` also passes (65 tests, OK, 5 skipped).

## Open next questions

1. Exact `cert(M)` for the worst instance (config, v = 7, seed `20262138`, `cert` in [6, 7]) by branch-and-bound over labellings; it is the natural place to look for sub-v certificates. No structural blocker, just a longer exact run.
2. Universal versus unit-attached readings of the quantifier: wire A3/A4/D4 Gram tables into the pairing-cost minimizer and compare admissible-B minima on the same decoders. Blocked on unit tables not being in this package.
3. The tied-minima family at v = 13..18, where the named obstruction accumulates.

## Credit and provenance

F-star, the `cert(M)` definition, L8 labellings and the proven chain are from the merged package `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` (root units, Lemmas A and B, the L8 lemma; [PR 1590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1590) by DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code assistance). The rank-3 configuration model and the `tied_min` / `cex_min_1` examples with their certificate limits are DreamingOfClouds' work in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162; this package neither restates those examples nor supersedes those results. The adjacent independent CR2/B2 audit is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2293 (Aaron Wang). The source README is pinned as an input in `SOURCES.json`. The coordination claim is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18941664.

Prepared by **Aaron Wang** with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). New work is Apache-2.0.
